chunks: And I asked him, "Can a fasting person perform cupping?" So he said, "I fear for him what he might fear for himself."
He said: I said, "What do you fear for him?" He said, "Fainting, or that bile may be stirred in him."
I said, "What if he is strong enough for that and does not fear anything?" He said, "Yes, if he wishes."

key_terms.قَوِيَ: he was strong or physically able
key_terms.مِرَّةٌ: bile; a bodily humor whose agitation may cause illness

ai.seo_question: Can a fasting person do cupping (hijamah) while fasting?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of hijamah for a fasting person. It indicates that cupping is not inherently forbidden during fasting, but it is discouraged if it may cause harm such as fainting or physical weakness; if the fasting person is strong and unafraid of harm, it is permitted.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: He said: "I asked him, 'Can a fasting person perform cupping (hijamah)?' Imam (as) replied: 'I fear for him what he might fear for himself.'
I asked: 'What do you fear for him?' Imam (as) said: 'Fainting or the stirring of bile.'
I asked: 'What if he is strong enough and does not fear anything?' Imam (as) said: 'Yes, if he wishes.'"
